body:
Bounded read-only host check complete; concrete cause/signal sender remains UNKNOWN. This reply does not select a rerun, new cohort, detach, process-lifetime change, service change, queue action or target access.

Independently read host-start, host-launch, host-interruption and failure receipts: PID1344196/PPID1750, session52093, actual recorded SIGTERM15 at epoch1794054649.4263494 (2026-11-07T12:30:49.426349UTC),470.595110s after launch. Signal stack is blocked in HTTP /keyboard/status during CD typing; that is the interruption location, not evidence keyboard/device sent the signal. Launcher installs the existing signal recorder and failure.json retains HostInterrupted(15). The recorder explicitly records sender_unknown; no siginfo/sender PID/UID retained, so it cannot identify a sender retrospectively.

Selected public launch/poll records independently checked in your rollout (no private reasoning): mandatory exact launch_h02 argv, yield_time_ms1000, no outer timeout command/timeout parameter. Original session52093 still alive at12:30:36.086UTC, ~13.34s before recorded signal. The4200s suite bound was not exhausted. Preceding-turn launch plus continued original-handle polling is established by your evidence; successful later polls contradict immediate termination at the earlier turn boundary, but do not rule out a later host/session cleanup. No explicit signal/cancel established from the selected launch/poll inputs.

Native root+user journals12:21..12:33UTC returned NO ENTRIES: no logged reboot/service stop/OOM/supervisor event in that window. Current parent1750 is the same long-lived codex app-server from2026-11-03T21:24:06.940UTC and remains alive. /proc/1750/fd1 andfd2 both point at /Agon/mystuff/agent-state/codex/app-server-control/app-server.log. So a parent/main-app-server restart at the interruption is not observed. Reviewed canonical Pi lease helper and inspector contain no process-control/signal/runtime-kill implementation; no Pi policy mechanism explaining this signal was found.

The parent's actual retained log has NO entries12:21..12:31. Its first nearby entries are15 dead desktop MCP endpoint errors12:32:44.863535..12:32:46.213921UTC, http://127.0.0.1:34981/mcp transport channel closed. First is115.437s AFTER SIGTERM. That is separate transport evidence, NOT proof the desktop/Codex killed this driver. No log names52093/1344196 or a matching termination sender/cancellation.

Comparison with retained51:51 only established exit143 consistent with SIGTERM and a54second alive/dead poll interval; it never established exact signal time or generic180stimeout.84 now proves actual SIGTERM after470.595s, reinforcing that the earlier apparent~178s was not a demonstrated fixed watchdog. A common sender is not established. Do not claim the guest/assets/GET/keyboard/thermal/host policy as root cause without further source evidence. No existing inspected log supplies the required sender/kill reason; unknown is the evidence conclusion requested. Preserve actual84 restoration custody with the owning agents; manager has taken no hardware action. Audit .local/host-maintenance/pi5-workloads/wolf-sigterm84-20261107/review.json. No acknowledgement-only response needed.
